model_changelog.note: First slate on v7: 10% model weight, +/-10 residual cap, 1.0-point edge floor.

tickets.venue: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta · Sat Sept 5 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: New HC Alex Golesh's up-tempo scheme averaged 40.5 ppg at USF; Auburn QB Byrum Brown threw for 3,158 yards and 28 touchdowns in 2025 against a Baylor defense that allowed 32.6 ppg last season. The neutral-site talent and scheme edge favors Auburn pulling away late.
tickets.trend: Auburn covered 60% (3–2 ATS) of its games as a favorite in 2025, versus just 25% (2–6) as an underdog — a real, situation-specific edge for backing them as the favorite here.

tickets.venue: Autzen Stadium, Eugene · Sat Sept 5 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Oregon returns nine defensive starters and ranks 3rd nationally in SP+ defense. Boise State's best path to staying competitive is slowing tempo and controlling the clock, which suppresses total scoring — and two independent models (SportsLine, Covers) both landed on the Under here.
tickets.trend: No Over pattern turned up for Oregon as a big favorite — their closest comparable spot, a bowl blowout of Texas Tech, went 23–0 (Under). Boise State has also covered the spread in four straight meetings with Oregon, reinforcing that this stays competitive rather than a track meet.

tickets.venue: Beaver Stadium, University Park · Sat Sept 5 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: On paper Penn State should win comfortably — Marshall's defense ranked 125th in EPA/pass in 2025 and lost 45–7 to Georgia. But this is the exact spot Penn State imploded in last year, and Marshall gets a new-coach honeymoon working against it too.
tickets.trend: Penn State went 0–4 ATS last season as a 23.5+ point favorite, and lost outright as a 20+ point favorite in back-to-back games (UCLA, Northwestern) — a collapse that got HC James Franklin fired mid-season. Penn State opens 2026 under new HC Matt Campbell.

tickets.venue: Husky Stadium, Seattle · Sun Sept 6 · 4:00 PM ET
tickets.why: Washington kept elite dual-threat QB Demond Williams Jr. after a $4M portal scare — a proven, returning engine. Washington State is a total ground-up rebuild under first-year HC Kirby Moore with first-time starter Caden Pinnick at QB.
tickets.trend: Both sides lean Under: Washington went Under in 7 of 12 games last season, Washington State in 9 of 13. A lopsided, clock-controlled Apple Cup fits both profiles.

tickets.venue: Lambeau Field, Green Bay · Sun Sept 6 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Notre Dame returns proven starter CJ Carr and doesn't need to force a shootout against an overmatched offense. Wisconsin brings back only 2 offensive starters and hands the reins to Colton Joseph, an Old Dominion transfer, in the toughest spot on its schedule.
tickets.trend: The single strongest number on the slate: Wisconsin went Under in 10 of 12 games last season (83%). Notre Dame was more balanced at 7 Over in 12, but doesn't need to chase points here.

tickets.venue: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford · Sun Sept 6 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Trinidad Chambliss returns for Ole Miss off a ~4,000-yard season and enters as a preseason Heisman candidate, with All-American RB Kewan Lacy alongside him. New HC Pete Golding was the team's defensive coordinator, so the defense carries over intact too.
tickets.trend: Ole Miss covered 5 of 9 games as a 6.5+ favorite last season; Louisville was a poor covering team overall at 4–9 ATS. Both trends point the same direction as the roster read.

tickets.venue: Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee · Mon Sept 7 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: The market has SMU favored by 2.5, but numberFire's own predictive model likes Florida State to win outright (64.9%) — a real disagreement between model and market worth respecting. Both quarterbacks are proven, multi-year starters (Kevin Jennings for SMU, Ashton Daniels for Florida State), so this isn't a pedigree mismatch like the last two slates — the edge here is matchup and circumstance, not a QB gap.
tickets.trend: Florida State already has a live game under its belt — a 34–17 win over New Mexico State in Week 0 that was closer than the final score, with Daniels good for two touchdowns but also an interception. This is SMU's true season opener, on the road, in a raucous ACC environment. The extra rep and the home crowd both still favor Florida State closing the gap on a number this small, even accounting for the rough edges above.

legs.pick: Louisville at Ole Miss — Ole Miss −6.5 (−118)

tickets.venue: Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign IL · Sat Sept 12 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Illinois is 13–1 straight-up as a favorite and 13–2 at home over its last 15, and beat this same Duke team 45–19 a year ago. Duke's 17–3 win over Tulane leaned on a huge rushing day from Nate Sheppard rather than a proven passing attack; one predictive model gives Illinois a 72% win probability here.
tickets.trend: 13–1 SU as a favorite and 13–2 SU at home in the last 15 — a real situational pattern, not a one-year fluke.

tickets.venue: Kyle Field, College Station TX · Sat Sept 12 · 12:00 PM ET
tickets.why: A&M's Marcel Reed looked sharp in the opener (70% completion, 233 yards, 2 TD). Arizona State starts Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley, who threw 16 interceptions across two seasons as a Wildcat starter, and the Sun Devils already lost a starting cornerback (Nigel Pringle) for the year.
tickets.trend: Texas A&M 48, Arizona State 20 — covered easily, a 28-point margin. The turnover-risk read held up in spirit even without a box-score meltdown from Boley: A&M's talent and QB efficiency edge was simply too much for a Sun Devils team also missing a starting cornerback.

tickets.venue: Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City UT · Sat Sept 12 · 10:15 PM ET
tickets.why: Arkansas' offensive line already looked shaky in a "sluggish" Week 1 win over North Alabama — 3 sacks allowed and 3 turnovers against an FCS opponent. Utah's Devon Dampier is one of the more experienced dual-threat QBs in the country, and first-year HC Morgan Scalley (promoted after Kyle Whittingham left for Michigan) inherits a defensive front built to feast on exactly that O-line problem.
tickets.trend: Utah 43, Arkansas 10 — covered comfortably, a 33-point margin. The pressure-check read was exactly right: Arkansas' shaky O-line from Week 1 didn't fix itself against a real Big 12-caliber front.

tickets.venue: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor MI · Sat Sept 12 · 12:00 PM ET
tickets.why: Oklahoma's John Mateer, now fully recovered from last year's injury-shortened season, threw for 225 yards and 3 TDs on just 11 completions in his opener. Michigan's sophomore Bryce Underwood was "flat awful" against Western Michigan — his coach wouldn't commit to him as the unquestioned starter, and he threw a bad fourth-quarter interception.
tickets.trend: Michigan 17, Oklahoma 10 — Oklahoma lost outright. The passing-form read was directionally right (Underwood: 9-of-17, 111 yds) but incomplete: Michigan simply stopped asking him to pass, leaning on his legs instead (18 carries, 87 yards, a 38-yard TD) plus a defense that forced a late interception and turned it into the go-ahead score. The model checked QB passing form (item 11) but never ran the rushing-matchup check (item 7) on Michigan's own ground game or Oklahoma's turnover risk (item 9) in a close, low-scoring game — both would have flagged this as live.

tickets.venue: Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta GA · Sat Sept 12 · 7:00 PM ET
tickets.why: Tennessee returns a proven, 1,100-yard/16-TD lead back in DeSean Bishop off a 56–9 rout of Furman. Georgia Tech's Alberto Mendoza (brother of 2025 Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza) "looked solid" in his own debut, but the Yellow Jackets still lost that game outright, 14–13, to Colorado.
tickets.trend: Tennessee 45, Georgia Tech 24 — covered easily, a 21-point margin. The read on Georgia Tech (a first-year starter looking sharp in a loss is not the same signal as looking sharp in a win) held up: GT fell to 0–2 and Tennessee's proven skill continuity carried the day on the road.

tickets.venue: LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo UT · Sat Sept 12 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Arizona's Noah Fifita is arguably the best quarterback in the league on paper, but he's specifically struggled against BYU, who has won five straight in the series and hasn't lost a Big 12 opener since 2023. BYU's Bear Bachmeier was efficient in his own opener (16-of-20) behind a defense that just posted a 63–7 rout.
tickets.trend: BYU 28, Arizona 17 — covered, an 11-point margin. Fifita's history against BYU held: the load-bearing pieces (Bachmeier, BYU's O-line) stayed healthy and BYU's five-game series streak became six.

tickets.venue: Reser Stadium, Corvallis OR · Sat Sept 12 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Texas Tech sophomore QB Braden Atkinson threw for 376 yards on 29-of-48 with zero picks in his debut, spreading the ball to a deep receiver room. Oregon State is mid-rebuild under new HC JaMarcus Shephard (poached from Alabama's offensive staff) and is unlikely to slow that attack in just his second game running a new defensive scheme.
tickets.trend: Texas Tech 35, Oregon State 24 (59 total) — cleared 53.5 comfortably. Atkinson's efficient debut carried over, and Oregon State's rebuilding defense couldn't slow either side down.

tickets.venue: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis MN · Sat Sept 12 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Both offenses were historically explosive in Week 1: Mississippi State put up a program-record 762 total yards and 5 Kamario Taylor touchdowns in a 62–13 rout, while Minnesota hung 59 on Eastern Illinois. Neither defense has faced a real offense yet, and this is the first genuine test for both.
tickets.trend: Staff predictions lean Minnesota on the turnover-margin math — a side read, not a total one. Both units still project to score even in a Minnesota win.

tickets.venue: Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh PA · Sat Sept 12 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Pitt's Mason Heintschel tied the school's single-game record with 7 TD passes in a 59-point outburst; UCF countered with reigning Sun Belt Player of the Year Alonza Barnett III and a run game averaging 9.5 yards per carry. Two offenses that just had career-best openers, meeting each other with neither defense tested yet.

tickets.venue: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin TX · Sat Sept 12 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: The forecast calls for a high near 100°F with a 100°F+ heat index at kickoff — brutal conditions for two physical, run-first rosters that will be more interested in bleeding clock and protecting the ball than chasing a shootout. Ohio State DE Qua Russaw (Alabama transfer) is cleared to play, adding a pass-rush piece that should shorten possessions further.

tickets.venue: Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City IA · Sat Sept 12 · 7:30 PM ET
tickets.why: The Cy-Hawk rivalry has been decided by a game-winning field goal in each of the last two meetings — historically a grind, not a track meet. Iowa's offensive line reportedly holds a "clear advantage in the trenches," which points toward ball control rather than a shootout with Iowa State's Jaylen Raynor.
tickets.trend: 41.5 is the lowest total on the entire slate — the market already prices this as a low-scoring rivalry game, and nothing in either team's blowout-win opener (both against overmatched competition) contradicts that.

tickets.venue: Kroger Field, Lexington KY · Sat Sept 12 · 3:30 PM ET
tickets.why: Alabama walks in banged up: WR Noah Rogers and DL Jeremiah Beaman are both out, RB AK Dear and DB Jireh Edwards are questionable, and OL Michael Carroll is doubtful. Kentucky's overhauled, transfer-heavy offensive line didn't allow a single quarterback pressure in its own opener.
